question: What are the hardware building blocks (Grace CPU, Blackwell GPU, NVLink, NVSwitch, NVL72 rack) of a modern AI system and what do they imply for power, cooling and utilisation?
contributions: Walkthrough of the GB200/GB300 superchip, Blackwell dual-die GPU, NVLink 5/NVSwitch fabric, NVL72 rack, power and cooling, and NVIDIA roadmap through Feynman (2028)

limits: No measurements by the author; all figures are NVIDIA specifications or NVIDIA-reported results with no citation printed
Roadmap sections (Rubin, Rubin Ultra, Feynman) are labelled partly speculative by the author
Internal inconsistencies: Grace bandwidth ~500 TB/s vs ~500 GB/s; GPU heat 1,200 W vs 1,000 W; NVLink latency 1-2 microseconds vs single-digit microseconds
The 30x token-throughput comparison mixes FP4, NVLink domain size and hardware; the chapter does not separate them
Hardware generation 2025; later parts (Rubin timing, power) will have dated
practices: Keep as much communication as possible inside the NVL72 rack (NVLink/NVSwitch) and use InfiniBand/Ethernet between racks only when needed (NVLink and NVSwitch section).
Explicitly manage placement and movement (asynchronous prefetch, staged pipelines) despite unified memory; keep hot data in HBM and use LPDDR5X for overflow (CPU and GPU Superchip).
Monitor GPU utilisation, NVLink throughput and power with DCGM; sustained 50% utilisation signals data loading or synchronisation stalls (Performance Monitoring).
Cap power or clocks for jobs that do not need full performance to improve performance per watt (Performance Monitoring).
Use MIG, SLURM or Kubernetes to share a rack across jobs and track goodput and GPU-hours (Sharing and Scheduling).
Plan facility power (redundant feeds), liquid cooling and floor loading before hosting an NVL72 (Compute Density, Liquid Cooling).
Use the Transformer Engine kernels and modules to apply FP8 and NVFP4 where accuracy holds; it is not fully automatic per layer in all frameworks (Tensor Cores and Transformer Engine).

terms.definition: a custom high-speed link called NVLink-C2C (chip-to-chip)
High-Bandwidth Interface, the 10 TB/s die-to-die interconnect joining the two Blackwell dies
NVIDIA hardware and software that adjusts mixed precision (FP16/BF16 with FP8/FP4) to preserve accuracy
Scalable Hierarchical Aggregation and Reduction Protocol: in-network reductions in NVSwitch ASICs
a fixed group of exactly 32 threads executing the same instructions in lockstep (SIMT)
Data Processing Unit: offloads, accelerates and isolates networking, storage, security and management tasks from the host CPU
Multi-Instance GPU: splits one physical GPU into hardware-isolated smaller GPUs
